feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.desc: Customers leave it in the Feedloop chat widget on your site. AI answers right away and hands off to you when it doesn't know.

classify.title: AI triage
classify.desc: Sorted into bug, UX issue, feature request, or question. Similar reports are grouped with one click.

fix.title: Fix PR
fix.desc: It reads your repository, writes the fix as code, and opens a pull request. A person approves what ships.

notify.title: Notification
notify.desc: The sender gets "It's fixed." By email too, if they left one.

phone.botStatus: Usually replies in a few minutes

phone.visitorMessage: My cart empties when I press Back on the checkout page
phone.aiReply: Sorry about that! I've flagged the cart emptying on Back to the team.
phone.fixedBody: The cart now stays when you go back. Check it out in today's update.

problem.lead1: It isn't that you won't fix it. You can't keep up.
problem.lead2: Customers are already telling you. The problem is what happens next.

buried.line: Product feedback gets buried under support tickets
buried.desc: You clear the urgent tickets first and the day is gone.

unsorted.line: Similar feedback piles up and never gets sorted
unsorted.desc: It grows in a jumble, and later you can't tell where to start.

unaware.line: Even after you fix it, the customer who reported it never finds out
unaware.desc: Nobody tells them it was fixed.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.lead: The seven questions we get most.

noBot.q: I don't have a chat bot running. How do I collect feedback?
noBot.a: Feedloop builds one for you. Enter your product name and URL to get your bot, then paste one script line and it starts taking customer messages right there. There is nothing else to prepare.

noDev.q: Do I need to know how to code?
noDev.a: If you can paste one script line into your site, you are set. Without a connected repository, everything from receiving messages to AI triage and customer notifications still runs. Fix PRs are the step for teams that connect a repository.

codeSafety.q: Does the AI change our code on its own?
codeSafety.a: No. Feedloop stops at opening a pull request. A person reviews it and decides whether to merge. The only GitHub permissions it asks for are Contents and Pull requests.

price.a: Feedloop is free during the beta. If you add your own API key there is no daily limit, and the only cost is the API fees on that key. Without a key, up to 100 messages a day run on ours. The Starter, Pro, and Agency plans on the pricing page belong to a PayPal sandbox demo store built for the hackathon: they show the payment agent at work, and no real money moves.

wrongAnswer.q: What if the AI answers wrongly?
wrongAnswer.a: It doesn't answer what it doesn't know. It hands the conversation to you. You can edit the knowledge it answers from in the dashboard at any time, and changes apply from the next conversation.

pick.a: Two things. First, details about the element the customer pointed at: its type and visible text, a selector and position that can find it again, an HTML skeleton of tags and attributes with the text removed, screen coordinates, and the page URL at that moment. Emails and token-like strings in these details are masked before saving. Second, when capture succeeds, a picture of the part of the page the customer was looking at. Only the Feedloop widget is left out, so anything else on screen, including values typed into fields, can appear in it. Only your team can view it, through links that expire after 10 minutes. It isn't sent to the AI or put into PRs or emails, and it's deleted after 90 days. If the customer removes the attachment before sending, the screenshot is deleted within two days.

channelTalk.q: We already use a support tool like Channel Talk.
channelTalk.a: Connect it to Channel Talk as is. You don't need to show a new chat widget: messages that arrive in Channel Talk are triaged the same way, and the notification goes back through Channel Talk when the fix ships.

final.title: Add Feedloop to your product
final.lead: Setup takes five minutes. When a fix ships, the person who reported it is notified.

footer.privacy: To improve the service, we record sessions and screen replays of visitors who aren't logged in, using PostHog. Input fields and the support widget are masked in recordings.
